# zlabrd

> Reduces the first NB rows and columns of a complex general M-by-N matrix A.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlabrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlabrd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlabrd(
    order,
    M, N, nb,
    A, LDA,
    d, strideD,
    e, strideE,
    TAUQ, strideTAUQ,
    TAUP, strideTAUP,
    X, LDX,
    Y, LDY
) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `nb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of leading rows and columns to reduce |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | `d` stride length |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | `e` stride length |
| `TAUQ` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideTAUQ` | `integer` | `TAUQ` stride length |
| `TAUP` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideTAUP` | `integer` | `TAUP` stride length |
| `X` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × nb</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `X` |
| `Y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nb</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDY` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Y` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows in the matrix A.
- `N`: The number of columns in the matrix A.
- `nb`: The number of leading rows and columns of A to be reduced.
- `A`: On entry, the m by n general matrix to be reduced. On exit, the first `NB` rows and columns of the matrix are overwritten; the rest of the array is unchanged. If $m \ge n$, elements on and below the diagonal in the first `NB`

  -   columns, with the array `TAUQ`, represent the unitary
  -   matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors; and
  -   elements above the diagonal in the first `NB` rows, with the
  -   array `TAUP`, represent the unitary matrix P as a product
  -   of elementary reflectors.

  If $m < n$, elements below the diagonal in the first `NB`

  -   columns, with the array `TAUQ`, represent the unitary
  -   matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors, and
  -   elements on and above the diagonal in the first `NB` rows,
  -   with the array `TAUP`, represent the unitary matrix P as
  -   a product of elementary reflectors.

  See Further Details.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of the first `NB` rows and columns of the reduced matrix. $D(i) = A(i,i)$.
- `e`: The off-diagonal elements of the first `NB` rows and columns of the reduced matrix.
- `TAUQ`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the unitary matrix Q. See Further Details.
- `TAUP`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the unitary matrix P. See Further Details.
- `X`: The m-by-nb matrix X required to update the unreduced part of A.
- `Y`: The n-by-nb matrix Y required to update the unreduced part of A.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `Y`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlabrd.ndarray(
    M, N, nb,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    TAUQ, strideTAUQ, offsetTAUQ,
    TAUP, strideTAUP, offsetTAUP,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    Y, strideY1, strideY2, offsetY
) → Complex128Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `nb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of leading rows and columns to reduce |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix (M-by-N, column-major) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` (in complex elements) |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Real diagonal elements (length nb) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Real off-diagonal elements (length nb) |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |
| `TAUQ` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Complex scalars for Q reflectors (length nb) |
| ↳ `strideTAUQ` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUQ` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAUQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAUQ` (in complex elements) |
| `TAUP` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length nb</sub> | **out** · Complex scalars for P reflectors (length nb) |
| ↳ `strideTAUP` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUP` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAUP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAUP` (in complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × nb</sub> | **out** · Output matrix (M-by-NB, column-major) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `X` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `X` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `X` (in complex elements) |
| `Y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nb</sub> | **out** · Output matrix (N-by-NB, column-major) |
| ↳ `strideY1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Y` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideY2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Y` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Y` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows in the matrix A.
- `N`: The number of columns in the matrix A.
- `nb`: The number of leading rows and columns of A to be reduced.
- `A`: On entry, the m by n general matrix to be reduced. On exit, the first `NB` rows and columns of the matrix are overwritten; the rest of the array is unchanged. If $m \ge n$, elements on and below the diagonal in the first `NB`

  -   columns, with the array `TAUQ`, represent the unitary
  -   matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors; and
  -   elements above the diagonal in the first `NB` rows, with the
  -   array `TAUP`, represent the unitary matrix P as a product
  -   of elementary reflectors.

  If $m < n$, elements below the diagonal in the first `NB`

  -   columns, with the array `TAUQ`, represent the unitary
  -   matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors, and
  -   elements on and above the diagonal in the first `NB` rows,
  -   with the array `TAUP`, represent the unitary matrix P as
  -   a product of elementary reflectors.

  See Further Details.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of the first `NB` rows and columns of the reduced matrix. $D(i) = A(i,i)$.
- `e`: The off-diagonal elements of the first `NB` rows and columns of the reduced matrix.
- `TAUQ`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the unitary matrix Q. See Further Details.
- `TAUP`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the unitary matrix P. See Further Details.
- `X`: The m-by-nb matrix X required to update the unreduced part of A.
- `Y`: The n-by-nb matrix Y required to update the unreduced part of A.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `Y`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import zlabrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlabrd';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const M = 4;
const N = 3;
const nb = 2;

// Using the standard interface (row-major `M`-by-`N` matrix `A`; `X` is `M`-by-`nb` and `Y` is `N`-by-`nb`):
let A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * M * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
let d = new Float64Array( nb );
let e = new Float64Array( nb );
let TAUQ = new Complex128Array( nb );
let TAUP = new Complex128Array( nb );
let X = new Complex128Array( M * nb );
let Y = new Complex128Array( N * nb );
zlabrd( 'row-major', M, N, nb, A, N, d, 1, e, 1, TAUQ, 1, TAUP, 1, X, nb, Y, nb );
console.log( d, e ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface (column-major):
A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * M * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
d = new Float64Array( nb );
e = new Float64Array( nb );
TAUQ = new Complex128Array( nb );
TAUP = new Complex128Array( nb );
X = new Complex128Array( M * nb );
Y = new Complex128Array( N * nb );
zlabrd.ndarray( M, N, nb, A, 1, M, 0, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, TAUQ, 1, 0, TAUP, 1, 0, X, 1, M, 0, Y, 1, N, 0 );
console.log( d, e ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLABRD`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLABRD reduces the first `NB` rows and columns of a complex general m by n matrix A to upper or lower real bidiagonal form by a unitary transformation $Q^H \, A \, P$, and returns the matrices X and Y which are needed to apply the transformation to the unreduced part of A.

If $m \ge n$, A is reduced to upper bidiagonal form; if $m < n$, to lower bidiagonal form.

This is an auxiliary routine called by ZGEBRD

### Further Details

The matrices Q and P are represented as products of elementary reflectors:

$$
Q = H(1) H(2) \cdots H(\mathrm{nb}) \quad\text{and}\quad P = G(1) G(2) \cdots G(\mathrm{nb})
$$

Each H(i) and G(i) has the form:

$H(i) = I$ - tauq \* $v \, v^H$ and $G(i) = I$ - taup \* $u \, u^H$

where tauq and taup are complex scalars, and v and u are complex vectors.

If $m \ge n$, $v(1:i-1) = 0$, $v(i) = 1$, and v(i:m) is stored on exit in `A(i:m,i)`; $u(1:i) = 0$, $u(i+1) = 1$, and u(i+1:n) is stored on exit in `A(i,i+1:n)`; tauq is stored in `TAUQ(i)` and taup in `TAUP(i)`.

If $m < n$, $v(1:i) = 0$, $v(i+1) = 1$, and v(i+1:m) is stored on exit in `A(i+2:m,i)`; $u(1:i-1) = 0$, $u(i) = 1$, and u(i:n) is stored on exit in `A(i,i+1:n)`; tauq is stored in `TAUQ(i)` and taup in `TAUP(i)`.

The elements of the vectors v and u together form the m-by-nb matrix V and the nb-by-n matrix $U^H$ which are needed, with X and Y, to apply the transformation to the unreduced part of the matrix, using a block update of the form: A := $A - V \, Y^H - X \, U^H$.

The contents of A on exit are illustrated by the following examples with $\mathrm{nb} = 2$:

$m = 6$ and $n = 5$ (m \> n): $m = 5$ and $n = 6$ (m \< n):

$$
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & u_{1} & u_{1} & u_{1} \\ v_{1} & 1 & 1 & u_{2} & u_{2} \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & a & a & a \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & a & a & a \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & a & a & a \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & a & a & a \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & u_{1} & u_{1} & u_{1} & u_{1} & u_{1} \\ 1 & 1 & u_{2} & u_{2} & u_{2} & u_{2} \\ v_{1} & 1 & a & a & a & a \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & a & a & a & a \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & a & a & a & a \end{pmatrix}
$$

where a denotes an element of the original matrix which is unchanged, vi denotes an element of the vector defining H(i), and ui an element of the vector defining G(i).

</section>
